page.overview:
What is Ninjutsu?

Ninjutsu (: wiktionary:忍術#Japanese|, "patience technique"; "endurance technique") is an overarching system of martial arts and tactics used by ninja. Ninjutsu is also called shinobi no jutsu (Japanese: 忍びの術, "technique of shinobi") or ninpō (kanji: 忍法, "ninja method").

Spying in Japan dates as far back as the 6th century during the . Skills relating to espionage and assassination were highly useful to warring factions in feudal Japan. praised the importance of spies and assassins in his book . Although originally not grouped under a single name, at some point the skills of espionage became known collectively as ninjutsu, and those who specialized in these tasks were called shinobi no mono (Japanese: 忍びの者, "person of sneaking"). A practitioner may also be referred to as ninjutsutsukai (Japanese: 忍術使い, "ninjutsu user"). Ninjutsu was developed by various families hailing from the and regions of Japan in the late 15th century. Throughout history, shinobi have acted as saboteurs, assassins, scouts, and spies and are notorious for their use of stealth and deception. There are several styles (: 流, "ryū") of ninjutsu that have been taught, such as the , the , and the . The Togakure-ryū was developed after a defeated samurai warrior called Daisuke Togakure fled to the Iga Province and later came in contact with the warrior-monk Kain Dōshi who taught him ninjutsu as a new life outlook and means of survival. Togakure-ryū largely lacks the strict organization that can be observed in other martial arts.

Ninjutsu ensured the survival of ninja in a time of violent political turmoil and from it sprung a recognized profession. Ninjutsu included methods of gathering information, techniques of non-detection, avoidance, and misdirection, such as , , , , and fighting techniques, including armed and unarmed methods, and archery. Using arson as a means of sabotage and castle infiltration were typical of a ninja. Since disguises were so integral to the work of a ninja, education on outside professions was included in ninjutsu training as well as teamwork with fellow ninja on the field.

Multiple ninjutsu manuscripts, such as the (1655), the (1675), and the (1681), were written by descendants of as well as by members from a branch of the Hattori clan known as the Fujibayashi clan. The Bansenshūkai used the earlier Kanrinseiyō, a three volume-long book about ninjutsu, as a source for its information. The legendary Kanrinseiyō's existence was only known through its mentioning in the Bansenshūkai as the Kanrinseiyō itself is missing. The second volume of not the original Kanrinseiyō, but a 1748 handwritten reproduction was found in a Kazuraki Shrine warehouse in December 2021.

Also known as: ninja arts, ninja training.
